question: What is a namespace?
correctAnswer: A namespace is a way to organise and group classes. Using namespaces avoids naming conflicts between classes.
answer1: A namespace is a way to organise objects and methods within a class, preventing conflicts between variables with the same name.
answer2: A namespace is a container that allows classes to share functionality and inherit from one another without creating naming conflicts.
answer3: A namespace is a special class structure used to group related classes together and control which classes can access each other.

question: In C# what does the "this" keyword refer to?
correctAnswer: "this" refers to the current calling object. You can use "this" to call other constructors in the same class.
answer1: "this" refers to the parent class of the current object and can be used to access inherited constructors and methods.
answer2: "this" refers to the class itself rather than a specific object and can be used to access static members of the class.
answer3: "this" refers to the object that originally created the current object and can be used to access its properties and methods.

question: What is a constructor?
correctAnswer: A constructor is a special method called upon an object's creation. A class can have multiple constructors that are differentiated by their parameters.
answer1: A constructor is a special method called when an object is destroyed. A class can have multiple constructors as long as each has a different return type.
answer2: A constructor is a method used to define the behaviour of an object after it has been created, and each class can only have one constructor.
answer3: A constructor is a special method used to initialise a class and can only be called explicitly after an object has already been created.

question: What is a Finalizer (Destructor)?
correctAnswer: A Finalizer is a special method that is called by the garbage collector and is used to clean up unmanaged memory.
answer1: A Finalizer is a special method that is called automatically when an object is created and is used to initialise unmanaged resources.
answer2: A Finalizer is a method that is called when an object goes out of scope and immediately releases all memory associated with that object.
answer3: A Finalizer is a method that must be called manually by the programmer to release managed and unmanaged memory before an object is destroyed.

question: What is Garbage Collection?
correctAnswer: Garbage collection is an automatic memory cleanup process that frees memory that has no connection to the program. It is used in C# and other languages.
answer1: Garbage collection is a process that automatically deletes unused classes and methods from a program to reduce the size of the compiled application.
answer2: Garbage collection is a process that identifies memory currently being used by a program and automatically moves it to a separate area for long-term storage.
answer3: Garbage collection is a manual memory management process where the programmer identifies unused objects and explicitly releases their allocated memory.

question: What is a property?
correctAnswer: A property is data within a class that is controlled by getters and setters.
answer1: A property is a private variable within a class that can only be accessed through methods defined specifically for reading and writing its value.
answer2: A property is a method within a class that is used to perform operations on data and can optionally return a value.
answer3: A property is a class member that stores data directly and automatically provides public access to the underlying variable without getters or setters.

question: What is inheritance?
correctAnswer: Inheritance is the feature of allowing a class to inherit the functionality of another class. The original class is known as the parent and the derived class is called the child.
answer1: Inheritance is the feature of allowing a parent class to automatically inherit the functionality of its child classes.
answer2: Inheritance is the feature of allowing classes to share functionality by copying the methods and properties of one class into another class.
answer3: Inheritance is the feature of allowing a class to use another class's functionality without creating a relationship between the two classes.

question: Why is inheritance useful?
correctAnswer: Inheritance is useful because it allows for code reusability and creates a natural logical hierarchy that can model real-world relationships, which in turn helps with the structure of a program.
answer1: Inheritance is useful because it prevents classes from sharing functionality directly and ensures that each class maintains its own independent implementation.
answer2: Inheritance is useful because it allows every class in a program to inherit from multiple parent classes, reducing the need to create separate implementations.
answer3: Inheritance is useful because it removes the need for objects and allows all functionality to be defined within a single parent class.

question: In C# how many classes can a single class inherit from?
correctAnswer: 1, because C# only supports single class inheritance.
answer1: 2, because C# allows a class to inherit from one primary class and one secondary class.
answer2: Unlimited, because C# allows a class to inherit from as many classes as necessary as long as their members do not conflict.
answer3: 0, because C# does not support class inheritance and instead requires interfaces to provide inherited functionality.

question: What is Polymorphism?
correctAnswer: Polymorphism is a language feature that allows a derived class to be treated and used like its parent class.
answer1: Polymorphism is a language feature that allows a parent class to automatically inherit all unique functionality from its derived classes.
answer2: Polymorphism is a language feature that allows multiple classes to have the same name as long as they belong to different namespaces.
answer3: Polymorphism is a language feature that allows a derived class to replace its parent class entirely while maintaining the same interface.

question: What is the benefit of polymorphism?
correctAnswer: Having polymorphism allows you to write general code for a base class that can be used on all derived classes using their unique overridden implementations.
answer1: Having polymorphism allows you to write separate code for every derived class, preventing the base class from being used directly.
answer2: Having polymorphism allows all derived classes to share exactly the same implementation, removing the need to override methods.
answer3: Having polymorphism allows a base class to automatically change its implementation depending on which derived class was created, without using overriding.

question: What is abstraction in programming?
correctAnswer: Abstraction is the idea that irrelevant implementation details should be hidden from users and only details allowing for functionality should be exposed.
answer1: Abstraction is the idea that all implementation details should be exposed to users so that they can directly control how functionality works.
answer2: Abstraction is the idea that a program should contain only one implementation of each feature so that unnecessary classes are removed.
answer3: Abstraction is the idea that implementation details should be copied into derived classes so that they can independently provide the same functionality.

question: What is the benefit of abstraction?
correctAnswer: Hiding implementation details allows for a more streamlined and robust way to use the thing that's being abstracted.
answer1: Exposing implementation details allows users to directly modify the internal behaviour of an abstraction, making it more flexible and robust.
answer2: Hiding implementation details ensures that the abstracted object cannot be reused by other parts of a program, reducing potential errors.
answer3: Abstraction improves a program by removing the need for classes to expose any functionality to the user.

question: What is the Abstract keyword used for in C#?
correctAnswer: It is used to declare a class as incomplete and to signal that it should only be used as a base class. All derived classes must implement any abstract methods using the override keyword.
answer1: It is used to declare a class as complete and prevent it from being inherited, while requiring any methods inside it to be overridden by child classes.
answer2: It is used to declare a class as incomplete and allows it to be instantiated directly, while giving derived classes the option to override its methods.
answer3: It is used to declare a class as a base class that cannot contain implemented methods and requires every member to be overridden by derived classes.

question: What is the benefit of the Abstract keyword?
correctAnswer: It allows you to enforce behaviour to derived classes without the base class having the ability to be instantiated.
answer1: It allows you to enforce behaviour on a base class while allowing the base class to be instantiated independently of its derived classes.
answer2: It allows derived classes to inherit functionality without requiring them to implement any behaviour defined by the base class.
answer3: It allows you to prevent derived classes from changing the behaviour defined by the base class while still allowing the base class to be instantiated.

question: What is an Interface in C#?
correctAnswer: An interface is a pure contract for a class that outlines what that class has to implement.
answer1: An interface is a base class that provides shared implementation for classes while requiring them to inherit its functionality.
answer2: An interface is a class template that defines how a class should be constructed but does not specify which behaviours it must implement.
answer3: An interface is a contract that automatically provides default implementations to any class that references it.

question: How are Interfaces and Abstract classes different?
correctAnswer: An interface doesn't have any implementation; this means that the class doesn't inherit any functionality from it. It's just a way to enforce behaviour. A class typically has a "can do" relationship with an interface, while a class has an "is a" relationship with an abstract class.
answer1: An interface provides shared implementation to derived classes, while an abstract class only defines behaviour that must be implemented. Interfaces represent an "is a" relationship and abstract classes represent a "can do" relationship.
answer2: An interface and an abstract class both provide implementation, but an interface is used for an "is a" relationship while an abstract class is used for a "can do" relationship.
answer3: An interface is primarily used to provide inherited functionality and state, while an abstract class is only used to enforce behaviour without providing any implementation.
